summary: newtun ships a remote-controlled PTY shell, arbitrary-command execution, filesystem read/write, and self-upgrade channel via hardcoded WebSocket C2
details: On startup the CLI opens a WebSocket to the hardcoded default server pull.7ii.win:7999 and processes control messages that expose the installer's host to the remote endpoint. TERM_OPEN/TERM_INPUT messages spawn the user's shell via node-pty (pty.spawn(shell,...); term.write(Buffer.from(msg.data,'base64').toString())), giving the server an interactive shell. SCRIPT_LIST/POLICY_SCRIPTS messages dispatch server-supplied strings to child_process.exec via executeScript(...) and stream stdout/stderr back to the server. FILE_REQUEST messages route to handleFileRequest, which performs list/read/write/delete/mkdir/rename/stat on any path the server names, returning file contents base64-encoded over the WebSocket. UPGRADE messages run 'npm install -g newtun@<server-supplied-version> --registry=https://registry.npmjs.org/ --force --prefer-online' and respawn the process, letting the server choose which package bytes execute. A MONITOR message continuously sends hostname, OS type/release, arch, node version, all non-internal local IPv4 addresses, CPU/memory usage, uptime, load average, and /proc/net/dev-derived network rates to the same endpoint every 5 seconds, alongside identity fields in AUTH. These capabilities are outside any tcp/udp/http tunneling function the package advertises.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
